Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. title: Audio Engineer, Live Video
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity.

The Global Events Studio Team creates exceptional live and recorded video for Press, Marketing, Developer Experience, and Communications.

About the Role

The Audio Engineer will be the senior audio authority for high-profile livestreams, broadcast-style productions, studio recordings, public venue events, and critical on-location shoots. This person will design resilient audio systems, serve as A1 when failures are immediately visible, and deliver exceptional spoken-word audio across live, recorded, remote, and AI-enabled production workflows.

In this role, you will:

- Own audio design and A1 execution for complex broadcasts, live stage events, podcasts, and critical film/on-location shoots

- Build and operate redundant program, stream, multitrack, camera, backup-recorder, and archival audio paths with real-time monitoring and recovery procedures.

- Mix full-duplex speech-to-speech audio between humans and AI models 

- Design, commission, standardize, document, and improve audio signal flow for studios, control rooms, event spaces, and portable production systems.

- Rapidly assess unfamiliar venues and design reliable systems around acoustic, power, network, access, RF, and footprint constraints.

- Lead rigorous preproduction: technical designs, input lists, patch plans, frequency plans, rehearsals, testing, monitoring, redundancy, and fallback capture.

- Diagnose and repair signal-chain, DSP, synchronization, routing, RF, networking, and hardware faults during live production.

- Lead audio crews and freelancers, challenge flawed technical plans, and communicate decisive options under pressure.

- Own multitrack recording, editorial handoff, backup, delivery, and archival workflows across professional formats and specifications.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

- 8+ years engineering complex live, broadcast, and studio production, including high-profile livestreams, public venue events, design, configuration, and programming of physical audio infrastructure, and critical on-location filming or streaming.

- Proven experience serving as A1 when failures are immediately visible and time for sophisticated workarounds is measured in seconds.

- Expert command of gain structure, routing, EQ, dynamics, automixing, feedback control, real time noise suppression, mix-minus, IFB, intercom, playback, comms, and latency management.

- Deep experience designing and troubleshooting redundant program, stream, multitrack, camera, backup-recorder, and archival audio paths.

- Advanced proficiency with networked audio and DSP systems such as Dante, AVB, SMPTE ST 2110, Q-SYS, Yamaha, and Shure.

- Strong IP-networking knowledge, including clocking, multicast, VLANs, QoS, and diagnosing failures across audio, control, and enterprise IT environments.

- Expert wireless-microphone and RF coordination skills across crowded, high-consequence production environments, including frequency planning, antenna distribution, and intermodulation.

- Ability to capture exceptional spoken-word audio for keynote presenters, executive livestream hosts, stage panels, podcasts, voiceover, remote guests, and acoustically difficult spaces.

- Advanced microphone selection and placement skills, including lavalier concealment, boom technique, room treatment, noise control, and feedback prevention.

- Ability to mix full-duplex speech-to-speech audio between humans and AI models for a variety of different event formats

- Fluency with broadcast encoders, embedded audio, streaming protocols, conferencing platforms, and external distribution endpoints.

- Expert-level understanding of room acoustics and a fundamental understanding of acoustic science.

- Demonstrated success diagnosing and repairing signal-chain, DSP, synchronization, routing, RF, networking, and hardware faults during live production.

- Strong multitrack recording,

The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

The mission of the Waymo AI Foundations team is to develop machine learning solutions addressing open problems in autonomous driving, towards the goal of safely operating Waymo vehicles in dozens of cities and under all driving conditions. As part of our work, we also initiate and foster collaborations with other research teams in Alphabet. AI Foundations areas that we are currently focusing on include reinforcement learning, learning from demonstration, generative modeling, Bayesian inference, hierarchical learning, and robust evaluation.

Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

 

You will:

• Research and develop novel visual and spatio-temporal reasoning methods for multimodal Perception Foundation Models using AV sensor data

• Design and implement post-training recipes-including Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL)-to improve perception generalization in long-tail autonomous driving scenarios

• Conduct large-scale experiments and ablation studies on autonomous driving benchmarks, with the opportunity to publish findings at top-tier AI/CV conferences (e.g., CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/NeurIPS/ICLR/ICML)

 

You have:

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field

• Hands-on experience & strong publications in perception, and/or LLM/VLM

• Knowledge of pre-training and post-training of the large foundation models

• Strong Python coding skills with expertise in modern deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)

 

We prefer:

• Experience with visual reasoning for LLM/VLM/robotics/driving

• Experience with RL training in LLM/VLM/robotics

• Experience with open-vocabulary perception

 

Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year - far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll join Ramp's travel team, which builds two products, Ramp Travel and Juno. Both integrate with a growing network of travel management company (TMC) partners. You'll be our expert on how those integrations work in practice: how content (search, booking and changes), payments, approvals, servicing and reporting flow between our products and each TMC.

You'll own the operational side of each partnership, from the day it's signed through every customer that goes live on it. You'll work closely with engineering, our customer success managers, and the teams that sign new TMC partners and bring in customers through them, but you won't own those commercial relationships.

Success means each new TMC goes live more efficiently than the last, mutual customers on each TMC go live faster and more smoothly over time as your playbooks improve, and the TMC servicing experience for Ramp and Juno travelers is seamless and delightful.

The travel team is small and building quickly across both products, so everyone works beyond the edges of their role. Alongside your core work, you'll help wherever the team needs it most.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Investigate with engineering when bookings, payments or data don't flow correctly, and see fixes through with the TMC.

- Create SOPs for TMC agents to ensure they deliver top tier support for travelers.

- Keep TMC partners up to date on product changes that affect them, and answer their agents' questions.

- Join partner review calls to represent day-to-day operations.

WHAT YOU NEED

- 5+ years in implementation, partner operations, technical consulting, or a similar partner- or customer-facing technical role, ideally in travel technology, SaaS or fintech.

- Corporate travel domain experience, such as working at a TMC or with GDSs (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport), NDC content, or travel mid- and back-office systems.

- Technical fluency to troubleshoot integ

You’ll review set and production design work and judge it: what works, what doesn’t, and why. You need professional experience designing or building sets for real productions, and clear written English.
Scope of Work

• Look at set designs, room setups or production concepts and judge which one is stronger for a given script, brief or budget.

• Flag problems that would show up on the day (a set that does not fit the shot, a material that looks fake on camera, items wrong for the period).

• Check that a design fits the story, the setting and the budget.

• Write a short explanation for each decision so a reviewer can follow your reasoning.

What we’re looking for

• Professional work as a production designer, set designer, art director, set decorator, assistant art director or theatre designer.

• Experience with real productions: scripts or briefs, budgets, builds, shoot or install days and working with other departments.

• Comfort with design tools such as SketchUp, AutoCAD, Vectorworks, Rhino or Photoshop, or strong hand drafting. Not all are required.

• Comfort explaining why one design works and another doesn’t.

• Clear written English.

How the selection process works

•
Complete the curation interview. It is a short conversation about your experience with exhibitions, collections and attribution. You don’t need to prepare, look at anything or write anything. Finishing it is what moves your application forward.

•
Review. We check your experience against what the project needs.

•
Onboarding and first task. If selected, you get the guidelines and start with an initial task, which is reviewed before you continue.

This role fits someone who thrives on accuracy, follow-through, and high volume, and who treats a missed deadline as a problem to prevent, not explain.

Agent Onboarding & Contracting : Own the end-to-end contracting process for every new agent entering MPA, from initial paperwork receipt through active production status. Agents should be able to get a clear status update without having to ask twice.

Certifications & Appointments : Own the certification and appointment lifecycle for every assigned agent, by carrier and by state. Maintain a forward-looking view of certification deadlines and renewal windows so nothing lapses unexpectedly. Initiate processes ahead of schedule, support agents in meeting completion timelines, and escalate non-responsive agents to sales leadership before a lapse occurs.

The Financial Crime Quality Assurance (QA) team at OKX is part of the Compliance Assurance function and is responsible for reviewing and rating the quality of AML Transaction Monitoring alert disposition and Financial Crime Investigations performed by the Global Financial Crime Investigations Team. We are a team of risk-focused compliance experts who independently assess investigation quality, promote consistency in decision-making, and ensure compliance with AML/CFT requirements, internal policies, and regulatory expectations. •
Quality Calibration & Internal QA Meetings - Participate in and facilitate regular QA calibration sessions to review complex or borderline cases, discuss grey areas, align on scoring methodology, and ensure consistency in quality evaluations across the QA team. Share key findings, emerging typologies, regulatory expectations, and best practices to improve review quality and reduce subjectivity.

•
Performance Monitoring & Reporting - Monitor investigator quality performance, analyze QA findings and recurring error trends, and prepare regular quality reports and dashboards. Identify systemic issues, emerging risks, root causes, and opportunities to strengthen controls and support management decision-making.

Coaching & Quality Improvement - Provide time
